body.statement: For any \(P\in\mathcal P_{\beta,d}(L,G,H,\underline f,\overline f)\) whose \(g\) is constant on \(\mathcal X\), every \(M\in\mathfrak M_T\) satisfies \(C_g(M)=O_g(X)=0\).  Hence every feasible policy has zero per-law normalized matching regret and, by Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:causal\text{-}regret\text{-}reduction}\), zero ex ante mean conditional design-variance excess relative to the covariate prognostic oracle.
body.justification: This reduction verifies that the frontier measures heterogeneous prognostic geometry rather than creating loss under a design-irrelevant score.
body.gap: It is the homogeneous-score reduction implicit in offline matched-pair optimality and serves as a required internal consistency check.
body.consumer: Applied users can verify that the cap is harmless when baseline prognosis is constant.
body.proof_tex:
If \(g(x)=c\) for all \(x\in\mathcal X\), then every edge satisfies
\[
\{g(X_i)-g(X_j)\}^2=(c-c)^2=0.
\]
Definition \(\mathrm{def:pair\text{-}cost}\) therefore gives \(C_g(M)=0\) for every \(M\in\mathfrak M_T\).  Taking the minimum in Definition \(\mathrm{def:offline\text{-}oracle}\) gives \(O_g(X)=0\).  Consequently \(T^{-1}\mathbb E_{P,\xi}[C_g(M_\pi)-O_g(X)]=0\) for every feasible \(\pi\).  The corrected Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:causal\text{-}regret\text{-}reduction}\) identifies this last quantity with \(T\) times the stated ex ante mean conditional design-variance excess.
